title: [Bug]: EAGLE speculative decoding crashes for multimodal wrapper architectures — load_eagle_model resolves lm_head from target_model instead of target_language_model
author: benmcconaghy-art

comments.author: nightcityblade
comments.body: Hi, I'd like to work on this. I'll submit a PR shortly.

comments.author: nightcityblade
comments.body: The current main branch already contains this fix from merged PR #47914 (commit 0d12618e98ff): get_target_lm_head() now checks target_language_model.lm_head before the top-level fallback. There is no remaining focused code change to make here, so I am stepping back and unclaiming the issue.

comments.author: benmcconaghy-art
comments.body:
Thanks @nightcityblade for having a look at this. Can confirm independently — pulled the current `main` branch source for `load_eagle_model`/`get_target_lm_head` directly (raw file, not just the PR description) and it resolves `lm_head` via `target_language_model` before falling back to the top-level model, which covers the `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` case from this report. Verified working in production against our original repro as well, via an equivalent local patch applied to 0.25.1 in the meantime.

Closing as resolved on `main`. For anyone hitting this on a release prior to whichever version first ships the fix: the one-line workaround is patching `load_eagle_model` in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/eagle/utils.py` to fall back through `target_language_model.lm_head` — see the repro/root-cause above for the exact mechanism.
